title: realloc(): invalid next size Aborted (core dumped) and malloc(): unsorted double linked list corrupted
body_html:
I'm trying to print certain lines from files to the console. I'm using a dynamically allocated array to keep track of lines i want to print and if more memory needed i realloc it.

void print_with_context(int* arr, char* file, int arr_size){
        if(arr_size == 0)
                return;

        FILE* stream;
        char* line = NULL;
        size_t len = 0;
        int line_number = 1;

        stream = fopen(file, "r");
        if(!stream)
                die("fopen");

        smallest_to_biggest_sort(arr, arr_size);
        int i = 0;
        while(arr[i] <= 0 && i < arr_size) //ignore negative lines
                ++i;

        while(getline(&line, &len, stream) != -1){
                if(i >= arr_size)
                        break;
                if(i > 0){
                        if(arr[i] == arr[i - 1]){
                                ++i;
                                continue;
                        }
                }

                if(arr[i] == line_number){
                        print_cwd(); //print current working directory
                        int success = printf("%s:%d:", file, line_number);
                        if(success < 0)
                                die("printf with context");
                        errno = 0;
                        int line_length = strlen(line);
                        int fwrite_success = fwrite(line, line_length, 1, stdout);
                        if(fwrite_success){
                                if(errno != 0)
                                        die("fwrite");
                        }
                        ++i;
                }
                ++line_number;
        }
        free(line);
        if(fclose(stream))
                die("fclose");

}

void print_regex(struct stat* file_info, regex_t* regex_line, char* file){
        if(!S_ISREG(file_info->st_mode))
                return;
        if(!regex_line)
                return;

        size_t nmatch = 1;
        regmatch_t pmatch[1];

        FILE* stream;
        char* line = NULL;
        size_t len = 0;
        int line_number = 1;

        stream = fopen(file, "r");
        if(!stream)
                die("fopen");

        int* arr = malloc(array_length * sizeof(int));

        if(!arr)
                die("malloc");

        int start = 1, line_found = 0, i = 0;
        while(getline(&line, &len, stream) != -1){
                if(regexec(regex_line, line, nmatch, pmatch, 0) != REG_NOMATCH){
                        ++line_found;
                        if(line_found > resize){
                                ++resize;
                                array_length += 2 * context + 1;
                                errno = 0;
                                arr = realloc(arr, array_length);// <= here fails with the error
                                if(errno == ENOMEM)
                                         die("realloc in print_regex");
                        }

                        start = line_number - context;
                        for(;i < array_length; ++i)
                                arr[i] = start++;
                }
                ++line_number;
        }

        print_with_context(arr, file, i);
        free(arr);
        free(line);
        if(fclose(stream))
                die("fclose");
}

It doesn't crash the first time reallocing. It always does crush when it tries to realloc for the 2nd time. When it reallocs just one time it doesn't crush in the function but it does crash in main() before finishing the program. One time I also managed to get the malloc(): unsorted double linked list corrupted error. So what exactly am I doing wrong here?

events.body_html: "Invalid write of size 4 at 0x109E25: print_regex (crawl.c:392)" <- that is the problem. Valgrind found the problem. Forget about realloc, and fix print_regex (crawl.c:392).
arr = realloc(arr, array_length); this is the line it is referring to, which is also in the code i provided above @user253751

My guess is that you are writing to the array out of bounds in the line

arr[i] = start++;

because the line

arr = realloc(arr, array_length);

is allocating insufficient memory.

Note that in the line

int* arr = malloc(array_length * sizeof(int));

you are allocating array_length * sizeof(int) bytes, whereas in the line

arr = realloc(arr, array_length);

you are only allocating array_length bytes, i.e. the * sizeof(int) part is missing.
@yad0: Are you sure? I suspect that arr = realloc(arr, array_length); is line 385 and that arr[i] = start++; is line 392. Otherwise, the Valgrind log you posted does not make sense to me.

the problem was highly likely the missing sizeof(int) in realloc(). i'm going to try out different outputs and see if i get the error again. if not i'm going to mark your answer as correct. i don't think its arr[i] = start++ because i have also checked it with a debugger multiple times and it never failed there. thank you

@yad0 do you understand the type of failure? the problem is that arr[i] = start++ overwrites some memory which does not belong to you (probably belongs to the memory allocator where it keeps its variables) and then next time you call the memory allocator all its variables have weird values so it crashes.
@user253751 yes, i do understand failures where you overwrite memory, which doesn't belong to you. in this case however the problem was indeed the missing sizeof(int) in realloc()
@yad0 yes, which caused realloc to allocate less memory than you thought, so the latter 3/4ths of it weren't yours even though you thought they were
